name: Billing
desc: Payments, invoicing, pricing, accounting, marketplace, fraud, and business intelligence.

resources.name: 5 things I learned while developing a billing system
resources.desc: A great introduction on all the various aspects of a billing system, from currency to invoices, including great illustrations on the logic of changing plans. All these topics are detailed in dedicated sections below.

resources.name: Open guide to AWS
resources.desc: Links to the *Billing and Cost Management* section which details the broad characteristics of billing for a cloud provider.

resources.name: Billed for ¥21,120, invoiced at ¥2,112,000 and paid ¥2,112,000
resources.desc: Get rid of integers and floats for monetary values. Use decimals. Or face the risks of anomalous x100 charges.

resources.name: Don't just roll the dice – Software pricing guide
resources.desc: Huge and complete collection of pricing scheme, with their psychological effect and impact on revenue model.

resources.name: Business Model Patterns
resources.desc: A list of 15 different ways to sell products and services.

resources.name: Axial - Business models
resources.desc: 38 models for inspiration.

resources.name: The Network Monetization Map: Aligning Incentives with Revenue
resources.desc: 6 models of monetization relying on network effect.

resources.name: The 5 Pillars of PriceOps
resources.desc: A manifesto inspired by the DevOps movement in which pricing is no longer ossified, but is practiced as a responsive iteration process, and implemented as a flexible property of the system.

resources.name: SaaS pricing explorer
resources.desc: A collection of 1000+ pricing pages for inspiration.

resources.name: Why I Love Usage-Based Pricing
resources.desc: “The most important reason I like this pricing model is that it heavily incentivizes both the customer and the service provider to act in everyone's best interest.” Also details issues with other pricing models.

resources.name: Use-cases for cloud services
resources.desc: The reason usage-based pricing makes even more sense for cloud services: to optimize ROI, keep all regular workload in traditional architecture and reserve cloud computing for elastic and experimental projects.

resources.name: Socially Optimal Pricing of Cloud Computing Resources
resources.desc: “The socially optimal operating point is unique, and can be sustained by a linear, usage-based tariff, which charges a fixed price per unit resource and unit time.” This paper justify usage-based pricing for cloud resources.

resources.name: A Survey of Profit Optimization Techniques for Cloud Providers
resources.desc: “The strategy of improving user service quality is discussed first, followed by the pricing strategy for cloud resources to maximize revenue.”

resources.name: Riemann sum
resources.desc: The starting point about quantization of usage.

resources.name: Allen's interval algebra
resources.desc: Implementing usage-based pricing is tricky, and this algebra will help you organize temporal reasoning. Also see this Stack Overflow question with clean schema.

resources.name: Reconcile Your Monthly GCP Invoice with BigQuery Billing Export
resources.desc: Behind the quest of this developer to track its expenses, you get a glimpse on cloud billing difficulties. While not explicitly pointed out, pricing cloud resources is hard and the result of quantization, granularity and rounding, between space, time and currencies.

resources.name: AWS EC2 T2 Instances Demystified: Don't Learn The Hard Way
resources.desc: An example of really tricky burstable instances which accrues and limits its own amount of CPU usage credits.

resources.name: “Designing billing for a service can be really challenging”
resources.desc: Personal anecdote on the design of the pricing plan for AWS Simple Email Service.

resources.name: Subscription-based pricing is dead: Smart SaaS companies are shifting to usage-based models
resources.desc: Usage-based pricing is more optimal and more fair: it “allows a customer to start at a low cost, minimizing friction to getting started while still preserving the ability to monetize a customer over time”.

resources.name: Electropedia: Tariffs for electricity
resources.desc: Before the cloud, there was another metered resource priced by its usage: electricity. Here is a detailed (and multi-lingual) taxonomy of its vocabulary from the International Electrotechnical Commission.

resources.name: Lago
resources.desc: 💸 Open-source metering & usage-based billing in Ruby. Lago SAS sells a hosted Cloud and Premium add-ons on top of the AGPL core.

resources.name: StripeMeter
resources.desc: 🆓 Open-source, Stripe-native usage metering in TypeScript. Reconciles computed usage against Stripe invoices for “pre-invoice parity”, with exactly-once processing and real-time cost projections.

resources.name: CGRateS
resources.desc: 🆓 An open-source, fast (50k+ CPS) and scalable (load-balancer + replication included) real-time billing for ISPs and Telecom Operators, written in Go. Vendor-neutral, support-only commercial model.

resources.name: Pricing low-touch SaaS
resources.desc: “In low-touch SaaS, the most common way packages are presented are as different columns in a pricing grid, with each column corresponding to a plan, offered at a different price, with differential access to features or maximum allowable usage along some axis interesting to the business.”

resources.name: Lotus
resources.desc: 🆓 Open-source project to manage pricing & packaging infrastructure. Lotus Inc. only sells managed hosting on top of the MIT core.

resources.name: f-license
resources.desc: 🆓 Open-source license key generation and verification tool in Go. Solo-maintainer project, no commercial offering.

resources.name: The Three Part Tariff
resources.desc: Beyond linear pricing, there is a place for additional platform fees and free-tiers in the pricing structure.

resources.name: Pricing Psychology
resources.desc: Which numbers should you use? How high should it be? Should it be rounded? This guide has 42 tricks to help you choose the best price.

resources.name: The 7 factors to consider when pricing your startup product
resources.desc: Pricing is an offensive tool to reinforce your product value and underscore the company core marketing message.

resources.name: The Anatomy of SaaS Pricing Strategy
resources.desc: Explain how to articulate the pricing of SaaS businesses around the product strategy.

resources.name: The cup-of-coffee pricing fallacy
resources.desc: Explains why it is a sloppy analogy.

resources.name: Changing the Pricing Model
resources.desc: A couple of ways to re-license your product.

resources.name: Jeremy Howard - From Predictive Modelling to Optimization
resources.desc: “In insurance, the price is the product. (…) How do I change price to make shitload of money?” Or how to deliver results (optimal price for a customer) instead of delivering data (calculating a customer's risk, which had been the standard approach used by actuaries previously).

resources.name: Gabor–Granger method
resources.desc: Used in surveys to determine the price for a new product or service. The results can be used to produce a demand chart and a revenue curve.

resources.name: Van Westendorp's Price Sensitivity Meter
resources.desc: PSM is a market technique for determining consumer price preferences. Allows for drawing a revenue curve to estimate the price point delivering the maximum revenue.

resources.name: Pricing niche products
resources.desc: “The most compelling argument against simply picking a price, though, is that it limits how much you can learn about your market.” Then the author setup vickrey auctions to discover price.

resources.name: Finding the max revenue price mark for digital products
resources.desc: “To find the optimal price that provides maximum revenue for your product you will need to field-test several price points; you then reconstruct the revenue curve and find the peak.”

resources.name: Personalised pricing and EU law
resources.desc: Some cases of price personalisation are prohibited in EU due to consumer protection and data protection rules.

resources.name: GCP Product Catalog
resources.desc: All GCP SKUs available as an API.

resources.name: Pimcore
resources.desc: 💸 An open-source UI and database to manage product metadata, written in PHP Symfony. Pimcore GmbH sells Enterprise Subscription, PaaS, and proprietary modules on top of the GPL/POCL core.

resources.name: Infracost
resources.desc: 💸 Cloud cost estimates from Terraform code, surfaced as a breakdown in the terminal or as a diff in pull requests before resources are provisioned. Infracost Inc. sells a hosted dashboard (Infracost Cloud) on top of the Apache-2.0 CLI.

resources.name: Cloudorado
resources.desc: 💸 A comparison matrix which use ECU (Amazon's vCPU) as a CPU power measure unit. Operated by Cloudorado as a commercial cloud-comparison product.

resources.name: EC2Instances.info
resources.desc: 💸 Easy Amazon EC2 Instance Comparison. Operated by Vantage as a free lead-gen surface for its commercial FinOps platform.

resources.name: Forecasting: Principles and Practice
resources.desc: “Comprehensive introduction to forecasting methods and to present enough information about each method for readers to be able to use them sensibly.”

resources.name: Transforming Financial Forecasting with Data Science and Machine Learning at Uber
resources.desc: Discusses how Uber apply data science and machine learning in their financial planning platforms.

resources.name: Time Series Prediction - A short introduction for pragmatists
resources.desc: Great introduction on how time series can be used to evaluate business problems.

resources.name: sktime
resources.desc: 🆓 Python library for time-series machine learning, governed by the Alan Turing Institute. See the forecasting tutorial and the differences between sktime and the Prophet project.

resources.name: Darts
resources.desc: 🆓 Python library for user-friendly forecasting and anomaly detection on time series, stewarded by Unit8 SA which only sells consulting around it (no paid library tier). Wraps a huge number of models, including Prophet. Great for experiments, but bear in mind that all the models in Darts expects that your data comes at a very regular interval, and make a lot of assumptions about their shape.

resources.name: Komiser
resources.desc: 💸 Open-source tool to stay under budget by uncovering hidden costs, monitoring increases in spend, and making impactful changes based on custom recommendations. Tailwarden sells a hosted SaaS on top.

resources.name: GCP Cost Forecast
resources.desc: An example of consumption trend line for resource consumption.

resources.name: How to save money on your AWS bill
resources.desc: “The biggest cost savings there are: 1. Turning things off that you're not using; 2. Then spot instances; 3. Then reserved instances.”

resources.name: Customized Regression Model for Airbnb Dynamic Pricing
resources.desc: This paper describes the pricing strategy model deployed at Airbnb.

resources.name: Papers we love: Auctions and Bidding
resources.desc: A collection of papers on bidding and auctions.

resources.name: Vickrey auction
resources.desc: Hinted by an HN comment, in which yes, “‘Asking people what they'd pay for and how much rarely works.’ (…) Using a Vickrey auction, similar to Google's ad auction mechanism, can elicit a person's maximum willingness-to-pay.”

resources.name: 19 Tactics to Solve the Chicken-or-Egg Problem and Grow Your Marketplace
resources.desc: “Which comes first, the supply or the demand? Chicken or egg?”

resources.name: A Rake Too Far: Optimal Platform Pricing Strategy
resources.desc: A bit of vocabulary: “In a casino, the term *rake* refers to the commission that the house earns for operating a poker game. (…) While casinos use the term *rake*, a plethora of interesting word choices exist which all describe the same thing – keeping a little bit of the revenue for the company that is running the service.”

resources.name: Incentive Engineering for Computational Resource Management
resources.desc: Paper exploring the “mechanisms for the allocation of processor time and storage that are compatible both with programming practice and with market mechanisms.”

resources.name: Pricing of Service in Clouds: Optimal Response and Strategic Interactions
resources.desc: “How should the consumer modulate its demand to optimize its profits? (…) How should the provider and consumer negotiate the specific pricing structure they will employ?” Covers non-linear models, tiered pricing, elastic demand, consumer et provider strategies.

resources.name: History of Spot Instances
resources.desc: From AWS's original auction-based market (2009-2017) to provider-managed pricing across all major clouds today. Documents how transparent bidding was replaced by opaque algorithms.

resources.name: Dynamic Cloud Pricing for Revenue Maximization
resources.desc: “Amazon's spot price is unlikely to be set according to market supply and demand. Rather, price oscillates within a very narrow band most of the time, which is more likely to be an artifact of some pricing algorithm with predetermined reserve price.”

resources.name: Usage Patterns and the Economics of the Public Cloud
resources.desc: “We examine the economics of demand and supply in cloud computing. (…) These results explain why fixed prices currently prevail despite the seeming need for time-varying dynamics. Examining the actual CPU utilization provides a lens into the future. (…) demand fluctuations would be on par with the three classic industries where dynamic pricing is important (hotels, electricity, airlines) and dynamic prices would be essential for efficiency.”

resources.name: Maximizing Profit of Cloud Brokers under Quantized Billing Cycles: a Dynamic Pricing Strategy based on Ski-Rental Problem
resources.desc: “The key idea of our algorithms is to use pricing signal to regulate user demand. One may argue that such an algorithm gives poor service to the user as it pushes tasks out of the queue in order to maximize cloud broker's profit.”

resources.name: Present or Future: Optimal Pricing for Spot Instances
resources.desc: “Pricing policy of spot resources should be carefully designed and the impact on both present and future should be considered.”

resources.name: Deconstructing Amazon EC2 Spot Instance Pricing
resources.desc: “Cloud providers possessing large quantities of spare capacity must either incentivize clients to purchase it or suffer losses. Amazon is the first cloud provider to address this challenge, by allowing clients to bid on spare capacity and by granting resources to bidders while their bids exceed a periodically changing spot price.”

resources.name: GCP Preemptible VMs vs AWS Spot Instances
resources.desc: “Google's prices are fixed, whereas AWS uses a market model”.

resources.name: The Eternal Cost Savings Of Netflix's Internal Spot Market
resources.desc: When you're big enough that creating an internal secondary market for instances makes economic sense.

resources.name: RTB Budget Pacing Summarized
resources.desc: A reading list distilling research papers from Turn Inc., Yahoo, and LinkedIn on RTB budget pacing techniques. Static resource: dated but still a useful entry point into the literature.

resources.name: Samsung's online ads platform/exchange war story
resources.desc: How to scale to 5M bid request/s, 2ms Max Response Time.

resources.name: RTB4Free
resources.desc: 🆓 Apache-2.0 OpenRTB 2.0-compliant bidder and Demand Side Platform (DSP). Largely dormant since late 2022, but the only OSS DSP reference in this niche.

resources.name: Accounting for Developers 101
resources.desc: A general introduction to history and vocabulary of accounting.

resources.name: Accounting for Computer Scientists
resources.desc: Describes how to view accounting in the form of graphs in which money flows, then how these movements are materialized in the financial statements of a small company.

resources.name: The Double-Entry Counting Method
resources.desc: Same premise as above, but way more detailed and complete, as it adds reporting and implementation details.

resources.name: Accounting Memento For Entrepreneurs (US GAAP)
resources.desc: An interactive form to play with accounting concepts.

resources.name: So, you want to learn Bookkeeping!
resources.desc: Focus on the daily operations of recording and maintaining the transactions of a business.

resources.name: Reconciliation: A game designed to frustrate the player
resources.desc: “Reconciliation is a business process which arises almost entirely because of a lack of structured data in the pipelines that convey money between businesses”. There are some hack to streamline the process, like adding an arbitrary discount to produce unique trailing decimals, or setup a couple of virtual bank accounts as proxy.

resources.name: Plain text accounting tools
resources.desc: Extensive list of open-source personal finance projects that might be great to look into for inspiration on double-entry accounting and bookkeeping.

resources.name: GnuCash Tutorial and Concepts Guide
resources.desc: A complete tutorial on personal finance tracking with GnuCash.

resources.name: Frappe Books
resources.desc: 🆓 Free desktop book-keeping software for small-businesses and freelancers, with no paid edition.

resources.name: Luca
resources.desc: 🆓 YAML accounting and JSON tax forms, solo-maintained.

resources.name: Blnk
resources.desc: 💸 Apache-2.0 double-entry ledger exposed as a REST API, with Go, TypeScript, Python and Java SDKs. Inflight transactions hold a pending leg until it is committed or voided, and the reconciliation engine matches external statements against custom rules. Blnk Finance sells a managed cloud adding back-office reports, audit logs and team permissions on top, but the core ledger, reconciliation and identity features are fully functional in OSS.

resources.name: Formance Ledger
resources.desc: 💸 MIT-licensed programmable double-entry ledger with the Numscript DSL, multi-currency, REST API, and Docker deployment usable standalone. Formance sells Enterprise add-ons (Wallets, Flows, Reconciliation, pre-built connectors, SSO, RBAC, audit logs) on top, but the core ledger is fully functional in OSS.

resources.name: Moonpig: a billing system that doesn't suck
resources.desc: Design decisions behind a billing and accounting system. Key takeaway: some companies still pays by checks; do not use floats; complex customer workflows; date and time issues; mutable data.

resources.name: Books, an immutable double-entry accounting database service
resources.desc: Explain the basic data model of a double-entry accounting system relying on Google Spanner for internal use at Square.

resources.name: TigerBeetle
resources.desc: 🆓 A distributed financial accounting database to ensure that the money either moves, or doesn't move, that it doesn't get lost somewhere in between. All features are in the Apache-2.0 OSS repo; TigerBeetle Inc. sells managed hosting and support, not gated features. It has been tested on Jepsen, which tested its strong serializability.

resources.name: Django Hordak
resources.desc: 🆓 Core functionality of a double entry accounting system for Django, single-maintainer MIT library.

resources.name: Managed accounts for Django
resources.desc: 🆓 A 'managed account' is an allocation of money that can be debited and credited. Community-maintained django-oscar extension.

resources.name: Triple‐entry accounting with Blockchain: How far have we come?
resources.desc: “Triple‐entry accounting is a new and a more efficient way to address fundamental trust and transparency issues that plague current accounting systems. Triple‐entry accounting with Blockchain, when properly implemented, can fundamentally improve accounting.”

resources.name: Tutorial on multiple currency accounting
resources.desc: An excellent resource for implementing multi-currency accounting systems.

resources.name: Accounts Demystified: The Astonishingly Simple Guide To Accounting
resources.desc: Helps you learn how to analyse and monitor your company's financial performance.

resources.name: The Games People Play With Cash Flow
resources.desc: “Malone created a new accounting metric, something he called ‘earnings before interest, depreciation, and taxes’, or EBITDA.” This is how a cable company CEO made sense of cash flow, like real-estate business did. The article starts with this example and describes other cash flow games for SaaS models.

resources.name: Financial Intelligence for Entrepreneurs: What You Really Need to Know About the Numbers
resources.desc: Allows you to fully understand how to use financial data to make better decisions for your business.

resources.name: What is FinOps
resources.desc: A framework for tech finance and business leadership teams to share the same language and processes of cloud operations and management.

resources.name: Algebraic Models for Accounting Systems
resources.desc: Advanced abstract algebra applied to the analysis of accounting systems.

resources.name: Is this what Enterprise mean?
resources.desc: When contracts, invoicing and payments are not working together, you end up alienating your big enterprise customers. See the associated HN comments on bulk license purchase.

resources.name: Entitlements untangled: The modern way to software monetization
resources.desc: “The concept of Entitlements encapsulates the feature access settings under various product variants (aka Pricing Plans or Packages), bridging the gap between how a product is sold and how it behaves for a variant. In essence, entitlements are a set of permissions defining what a customer (paying or non-paying) can do with your software application.”

resources.name: CUDs vs. Commit Contracts vs. SUDs in Google Cloud
resources.desc: Explains the differences between various types of discounts and usage commitments in GCP.

resources.name: Quantity discounts on a virtual good: The results of a massive pricing experiment
resources.desc: “Implementing price reductions ranging from 9–70% for large purchases, we found remarkably little impact on revenue, either positively or negatively.” If discounts are a placebo and are still widely used in the industry, maybe they are a marketing hack to lure big customers?

resources.name: Raising Prices is Hard
resources.desc: Backblaze post-mortem on raising prices on their main offer. They wanted to create an extension program based on credit system. This became a full-time job for a handful of their most senior engineers, and resulted in a six month project.

resources.name: Details on Expiring DigitalOcean Credits
resources.desc: The reason you have to add an time limit on credits: unused ones accounts as liabilities on our balance sheet.

resources.name: Hacking Scooters: How I Created \$100k Worth Of Free Rides
resources.desc: A cautionary tale on how promo codes can be exploited to get unlimited free rides.

resources.name: China’s Pinduoduo reports theft of online discount vouchers to police
resources.desc: The next level of fraud: “an online collective exploited a loophole on its platform to ‘steal’ tens of millions of yuan worth of discount vouchers”.

resources.name: Council Directive 2016/1065 as regards the treatment of vouchers
resources.desc: European directive on the application of VAT when vouchers are involved.

resources.name: The coupon code is a slap in the face
resources.desc: Point the negative consequences of users encountering a blank coupon field without having a coupon. See the update at the end of the article with research backing up this anecdote.

resources.name: 2017 Tax Software Developer's Guides
resources.desc: A list of test cases for developers to test their tax code against.

resources.name: {Digital,Cloud,Electronic,Online} Services VAT Rate Database
resources.desc: 🆓 Centralize applicable VAT rates on foreign online services, for each country of residence (including territorial exceptions).

resources.name: Global VAT & GST on digital services
resources.desc: List of countries requiring application of taxes on foreign provided online services.

resources.name: Streamlined Sales Tax Governing Board
resources.desc: A multi-states US initiative to automate and standadize sales tax accounting and collection.

resources.name: How to correctly setup SaaS subscriptions to charge VAT in Europe
resources.desc: “If you think you can just setup a simple Stripe integration and move on, like us, you'd be sadly mistaken.”

resources.name: Council Directive 2006/112/EC
resources.desc: European Union reference on the common system of VAT.

resources.name: What does the "Reverse Charge" refer to?
resources.desc: Answer: a provision in which a business transfer the responsibility of VAT handling to the customer.

resources.name: On GCP invoiced billing
resources.desc: Invoiced billing is a B2B-friendly payment happening after the service is consumed and an invoice issued. It seems to be a pain to setup on GCP but I suspect is a consequence of trying to reduce (costly) fraud.

resources.name: Content of EU invoices
resources.desc: The information required on a EU invoice is detailed by Article 226, Section 4 (Content of invoices) of Council Directive 2006/112/EC on the common system of VAT.

resources.name: Digital signatures: how Sleek leverages Cloud HSM to guarantee the integrity of legal documents
resources.desc: Here is a great way to rely on GCP's HSM to digitally sign documents and provide an immutable audit-trail. Might be applied to invoices as well as contract agreements.

resources.name: OpenTimestamps
resources.desc: Go beyond the solution above, and timestamp immutable document directly on Bitcoin's blockchain.

resources.name: Credit note
resources.desc: Because an invoice is immutable, the only way to fully or partially cancel it is to produce a credit note.

resources.name: Invoice Builder
resources.desc: 🆓 Offline-first desktop app to create, manage and export invoices and quotes to PDF, with all data kept in a local database you own.

resources.name: InvoicePlane
resources.desc: 🆓 A self-hosted open-source application for managing your invoices, clients and payments. Community project, no paid edition.

resources.name: klirr
resources.desc: 🆓 Zero-maintenance FOSS CLI tool for generating beautiful invoices for services and expenses.

resources.name: InvoiceGenerator
resources.desc: 🆓 Python library to generate simple invoices.

resources.name: microinvoice
resources.desc: 🆓 Fast Node.js library to generate PDF invoices with PDFKit, no headless browser required.

resources.name: Ruby Invoicing Framework
resources.desc: 🆓 For generating and displaying invoices (ideal for commercial Rails apps). It allows for flexible business logic; provides tools for tax handling, commission calculation etc.

resources.name: InvoiceNet
resources.desc: 🆓 Deep neural network to extract intelligent information from invoice documents.

resources.name: Invoice Security Vulnerabilities
resources.desc: European Union introduced a "standard" in XML format, which comes with a set of security vulnerabilities.

resources.name: EU eInvoicing
resources.desc: European standard on electronic invoice.

resources.name: Factur-X
resources.desc: 🆓 Python library to support the e-invoicing standard for France and Germany.

resources.name: Universal Business Language
resources.desc: Most invoicing software can read and write UBL documents (XML) for data transfer.

resources.name: GOBL
resources.desc: 💸 JSON Schema, Open Source Go library, global tax database, with conversion tools, all in one. Invopop sells a managed e-invoicing SaaS implementation on top of the open spec.

resources.name: The Best Payment Gateway for Startups
resources.desc: A benchmark of top payment providers, their pricing and models.

resources.name: Avoiding Double Payments in a Distributed Payments System
resources.desc: RDBMS were build for banks around transactions to solve that specific issue. Then NoSQL came forcing us to carefully implement systems to avoid double spending.

resources.name: Monzo's bank transfers post-mortem
resources.desc: Or why you should be prepared for and work around gateway provider's outages.

resources.name: How to Build an Insurance Company
resources.desc: The importance of payment ops architecture.

resources.name: EU's Late Payment Directive
resources.desc: European rules on applicable fees for late payments.

resources.name: High failure rate of Point Of Sale devices in the upper Midwest
resources.desc: The root cause? People wearing a lot of wool in low humidity air, generating a lot of static.

resources.name: Handling system failures during payment communication
resources.desc: Dropbox's experience trying to account for an unreliable payment provider.

resources.name: Why was I charged?
resources.desc: Under a constant stream of user complaints about payments, WordPress created a dedicated subdomains to help customers understand unexpected transactions. The trick was to add this URL directly in the bank statement.

resources.name: Hyperswitch
resources.desc: 💸 Open-source backend for payment processing. Juspay sells Hyperswitch Cloud and a self-host Enterprise edition; the OSS is functionally complete with 90+ connectors, vault, routing, 3DS, and fraud orchestration.

resources.name: Polar
resources.desc: 💸 Open-source monetization platform to sell SaaS and digital products. Polar Software Inc. runs the hosted polar.sh service as the merchant of record, handling billing, sales tax and VAT remittance for a cut of each transaction; the self-hostable OSS ships the full stack (checkout, subscriptions, usage metering, license keys) on top of your own Stripe account.

resources.name: moov
resources.desc: 🆓 Suite of Apache-2.0 libraries for financial technology, including moov-io/ach, iso8583, and watchman. No paid product on top.

resources.name: Fintech Open Source Foundation
resources.desc: 🆓 Linux Foundation project hosting open-source projects for financial services.

resources.name: The humble receipt gets a brilliant redesign
resources.desc: When a Netflix data engineer revisit receipts.

resources.name: The long, long history of long, long CVS receipts
resources.desc: “CVS is a drugstore much like other drugstores, with one important difference: The receipts are very long.”

resources.name: 'Is that even legal?': Companies may be sharing new credit or debit card information without you knowing
resources.desc: Some credit and debit card companies have "updating service" that allows new account numbers and expiry dates to be shared with merchants. Visa's implementation is called VAU and Mastercard's is ABU.

resources.name: Strong Customer Authentication
resources.desc: Payment Services Directive 2, explained.

resources.name: Address Verification System
resources.desc: A system checking the matching of customer's billing addresses with the one associated with the credit card.

resources.name: A (shallow) dive into the American banking system
resources.desc: Collection of miscellaneous notes primarily focused on the common cases of routable accounts, i.e. checking and savings.

resources.name: Open IBAN
resources.desc: 🆓 Free and public IBAN validation and calculation webservice.

resources.name: Swift Codes
resources.desc: Swift / BIC codes for personal use only.

resources.name: Swift Codes Repository
resources.desc: 🆓 Static JSON dataset of SWIFT/BIC codes for banks worldwide, scraped from the site above. Last refreshed in 2019 but still the largest free reference; SWIFT codes change slowly so the data remains broadly usable.

resources.name: EPC QR code
resources.desc: EU standard for QR codes used to transfer money between bank accounts via SEPA.

resources.name: UPI 101: The Basics
resources.desc: “In this article, we will learn about India's Unified Payments Interface. A four-year-old payment scheme that has been accounting for 40-45% of digital payments across India.”

resources.name: 20 years of payment processing problems
resources.desc: A huge collection of everything that went wrong, and still is, with payment APIs from the past 2 decades. Any issue exposed in this article that gets unaddressed will end up as stolen money.

resources.name: The untold story of Stripe
resources.desc: In which we learn that “once turnover hit a certain level, Paypal automatically put the business on a 21 to 60 day rolling reserve, meaning that up to 30 per cent of a company's revenue could be locked up for up to two months.”

resources.name: Idempotency in the context of payments
resources.desc: “Idempotency prevents race conditions. Idempotency dictates that multiple identical requests from the same client do not result in a different final state.”

resources.name: Optimizing payments with machine learning
resources.desc: Describes a classic payment workflow, then how machine learning can replace hard-coded business rules and fine-tune the payment failures/retries loop to increase the success rates of charges.

resources.name: Detecting fraudulent activity in a cloud using privacy-friendly data aggregates
resources.desc: Discusses a method to detect fraudulent activity (launching DDoS attacks, Bitcoin mining, …) by using non-intrusive, privacy-friendly data: billing data.

resources.name: Awesome List of IAM: Fraud links
resources.desc: Section dedicated to fraud management related to user accounts, from our sister repository.

resources.name: Driving Global Fraud Losses Down While Empowering Business Growth
resources.desc: In this talk by Uber Eats, we learn from the biggest payment processor that “growing businesses with declining loss rates is extremely rare in the industry”. Also, fraud can takes several forms: chargebacks on non-perishable goods, promo abuse, refunds…

resources.name: KYC and AML: beyond the acronyms
resources.desc: KYC is nuanced and fuzzy, because it is a stochastic process to reduce risk.

resources.name: Awesome Fraud Detection Research Papers
resources.desc: Papers sourced from several conferences on all sort of fraud: credit card, payment transactions, loans, customs inspections, money laundering networks, and more.

resources.name: Tazama
resources.desc: 🆓 Open-source real-time transaction monitoring software for fraud and money laundering detection, governed by the Tazama Linux Foundation project. This is just an engine to define rules, weight them, and apply them to transactions. There is nothing specific to payments or financial transactions.

resources.name: Mojaloop Fraud Risk Management
resources.desc: 🆓 Concrete AML rule implementations from the Mojaloop Foundation: transaction mirroring (90-100% amount-match window), multi-tier payee-graph traversal for layering detection, account-dormancy reactivation, large-transaction-payer, new-payee-transfer. Repo is archived but the rules are static reference material rarely seen elsewhere in OSS.

resources.name: Reproducible Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud detection
resources.desc: A practical handbook on how to identify patterns in transactions.

resources.name: How I Stopped a Credit Card Thief From Ripping Off 3,537 People – and Saved Our Nonprofit in the Process
resources.desc: Describe a fraud technique known as "card testing", in which massive batch of stolen cards are checked for their validity against your API.

resources.name: How Candy Japan got credit card fraud somewhat under control
resources.desc: Suggestions involved either warning signals for trying to guess which orders might be fraud, or countermeasures to try to make things harder for the fraudsters.

resources.name: Five Fun Fraud Facts
resources.desc: Another tiny collection of features we can feed to a ML system to detect fraud. Comments on HN also unearthed more qualifying signals and derived geodata on the transaction.

resources.name: Credit Card Fraud Detection using Autoencoders in Keras
resources.desc: Tutorial on how to rely on anomaly detection to implement suspicious card transactions.

resources.name: Training an ML model to score chargebacks
resources.desc: An example of a platform's network effect, which allows to predict the likelihood of winning a dispute.

resources.name: How credit card thieves use free-to-play apps to launder gains
resources.desc: To prevent abuses, service provider must strengthen both credit card verification and the account creation process.

resources.name: GCP improved account management policies to better support customers
resources.desc: Or why relying too much on fraud automation might lead to disgruntled users.

resources.name: Digital Ocean's Update on Customer Shutdown Incident
resources.desc: Aggressively shutting down user servers is good from a business point of view to prevent fraudster abusing free resources, until it's not.

resources.name: Awesome Credit Modeling
resources.desc: How to use statistical methods to classify applicants into categories to reduce risks. Lots of inspiration and research papers there to improve general scoring.

resources.name: Benford's law
resources.desc: Digit distribution can be a signal of accounting fraud.

resources.name: Integer percentages as electoral falsification fingerprints
resources.desc: In the same spirit as above, this paper show that frequency of reported round numbers in election is a signal of man-made anomalies. Might be applicable in some fraud-fighting area.

resources.name: Huber loss
resources.desc: “A loss function used in robust regression, that is less sensitive to outliers in data than the squared error loss.”

resources.name: Peak Detection in the Python World
resources.desc: Simple way to detect outliers.

resources.name: Method to check if you swapped 2 digits
resources.desc: Standard manual accounting trick employed when isolating an error in a double ledger.

resources.name: More than 600 million users installed Android 'fleeceware' apps from the Play Store
resources.desc: A new kind of fraud, in which apps silently keep charging users after the end of the trial period.

resources.name: CEO Fraud
resources.desc: A billing team responsible for collecting payment is prey to this kind of fraud, in which the CEO is impersonated to commend exceptional payment transactions.

resources.name: The Challenges of Operating a Computing Cloud and Charging for its Use
resources.desc: Skip the first 90% of this presentation by an AWS VP (which is about general system reliability). The last four slides are a good summary of what billing cloud services entails, especially the use of soft quotas to limit fraud.

resources.name: Fraud in Telephony Networks
resources.desc: Most of telephony frauds gravitates around billing and the metering of micro-transactions. This paper feature a taxonomy (on page 6) differentiating the root causes, vulnerabilities, exploitation techniques, and the way fraudsters can benefits from them.

resources.name: Apple In-app purchase Human Interface Guidelines
resources.desc: Guide and recommendation on how to make auto-renewable subscriptions user-friendly.

resources.name: Which has a higher conversion rate: A single long ecommerce checkout form or a multi-step one?
resources.desc: Focus first on other things in the cart, like easing anxiety and second-guessing by adding reassurance (trust marks, testimonials) near the credit card and completion steps, as well as some guarantee language that you may have used earlier in the product exploration process.

resources.name: We tried to make billing backendless
resources.desc: Failed attempt to move the billing experience by from backend to frontend because of security.

resources.name: Pricing pages design
resources.desc: A collection of pricing pages from various SaaS companies, to get inspiration on how to present your offers.

resources.name: Startup financial models - 12 templates compared for SaaS
resources.desc: A great source of inspiration to get better visibility in your operations.

resources.name: 16 Startup Metrics
resources.desc: The 2 critical metrics being Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Customer Lifetime Value (CLV).

resources.name: Thinking about growth and profit
resources.desc: Discuss the relationship between investments, profit and growth, and how it influence decisions on pricing, free trials and plan structure.

resources.name: A Quantitative Approach to Product Market Fit
resources.desc: Metrics produced above have a greater reach, as they're used as important signals to validate product-market fit.

resources.name: Startup growth calculator
resources.desc: Simple yet effective interactive profitability calculator for startups.

resources.name: An Overview of Visa
resources.desc: Great breakdown of Visa business models and metrics.

resources.name: The SaaS Financial Model You'll Actually Use
resources.desc: A complete tour of the financials of a startup, which gives you extra-context on how the metrics you produce fit into the larger picture.

resources.name: You're all calculating churn rates wrong
resources.desc: “On the surface, churn rate may seem like a natural proxy for changes in customer lifetimes. Let's dig into why that is not true.” Churn rate is not a meaningful metric to compute CLV: during the customer lifetime, the churn probability is not constant. Most of the time because of your free trial and vouchers. This article illustrate the influence of the distribution used to model the probability of a customer quitting.

resources.name: How to project customer retention
resources.desc: A seminal paper, with a stronger approach compared to the one above: the exponential distributions is replaced by a geometric model, which is better suited to discrete time intervals like monthly contracts, the former being more appropriate to continuous time process.

resources.name: Survival Analysis For Customer Retention
resources.desc: Illustrates how retention can be better modelled using a survival function like Kaplan–Meier survival curves.

resources.name: RFM (customer value)
resources.desc: A refined model of CLV, used to segment users based on Recency, Frequency and Monetary value.

resources.name: Churn Prediction
resources.desc: “How to use Python in a simplistic way to fuel your company's growth by applying the predictive approach to all your actions.” Relies on XGBoost binary classification.

resources.name: PyMC-Marketing
resources.desc: 🆓 A full-featured Python package to analyze your users based on their "alive" and "dead" states. Apache-2.0 library stewarded by PyMC Labs, which only sells consulting services around it (no paid library tier).

resources.name: AI vs Data Science vs Data Engineering
resources.desc: “Data Engineers build data pipelines and infrastructure to ensure a constant availability of transformed data. Data Scientists analyze and build models from these data to develop new product features or drive the bottom line of the business.” As for AI professionals, their focus is on cognitive automation.

resources.name: Ten Ways Your Data Project is Going to Fail
resources.desc: You don't need data scientists. “For ETL, hire data engineers. For reporting, hire BI analysts. The end.”

resources.name: Cargo cult data science
resources.desc: “Data science is best viewed as a form of company culture, rather than a set of technologies. However, many firms will try to create that company culture by acquiring data-science technology, rather than working on their culture.”

resources.name: Why not use Double or Float to represent currency?
resources.desc: Because of precision: floats and doubles cannot accurately represent the base 10 multiples that we use for money.

resources.name: Never Use Floats for Money
resources.desc: “This is precisely the problem we have when trying to represent 10^-1, or 0.1 in binary. There is not an exact binary representation of 0.1 or 0.01.”

resources.name: The Soul of an Old Machine: Revisiting the Timeless von Neumann Architecture
resources.desc: Floats were suspicious even before the first general-purpose computer (EDVAC) was built: “Von Neumann wasn't entirely sold on why we might need floating-point numbers. He was quite vocal in his critique of floating-point numbers.” The author of this article complement this critique by illustrating the issue of precision and rounding.

resources.name: European Spreadsheet Risks Interest Group - Horror Stories
resources.desc: A collection of cases in which uncontrolled and untested spreadsheet models led to lost revenue, mispricing, poor decision making, fraud and systemic financial failure.

resources.name: Practical Business Python
resources.desc: A blog collecting and spreading ideas on how to use Python more effectively in the business setting.

resources.name: redash
resources.desc: 🆓 Connect and query your data sources, build dashboards to visualize data and share them with your company. Owned by Databricks but the hosted SaaS shut down in 2021, so the project is now community-maintained under the Databricks org with no paid Redash product.

resources.name: Apache Superset
resources.desc: 🆓 Enterprise-ready business intelligence web application, governed by the Apache Software Foundation.

resources.name: Meltano
resources.desc: 🆓 Open source convention-over-configuration product for the whole data lifecycle, all the way from loading data to analyzing it. Meltano only sells managed Cloud hosting and support SLA on top of the OSS core.

resources.name: Patents on billing systems of the dot-com era
resources.desc: All of them have been abandoned and constitute prior art. This means there is nothing to prevent anybody to implement or commercialize these concepts.

resources.name: AWS Cost Management announcements
resources.desc: The source of all new features added to the billing perimeter.

resources.name: AWS reserved instances vs saving plan
resources.desc: A feature matrix of the different scheme and their average dicounts.

resources.name: GCP billing release notes
resources.desc: Latest changes of GCP billing features.

resources.name: GCP billing news
resources.desc: From the unofficial Google Cloud Platform newsletter.

resources.name: More choice, less complexity: New Compute Engine pricing options on tap
resources.desc: A wrap-up of recent GCP pricing features.

resources.name: Orbitera
resources.desc: GCP's billing subsidiary.

resources.name: DigitalOcean Billing changelog
resources.desc: All the latest billing updates on DO.

resources.name: Product Development as Iterated Taste
resources.desc: AWS sacrificed the simplicity of subscription pricing for S3 and went instead with a safe cost-following strategy because they had no clue how the users will use their service.

resources.name: Israel demanded Google and Amazon use secret 'wink' to sidestep legal orders
resources.desc: Invoicing of random fees with coded amounts were used as a hidden signal to bypass legal obligations. Maybe that's why you need a flexible billing system after all.

resources.name: £sd computing
resources.desc: The IBM 1401 mainframe (1959) optionally supported pounds/shillings/pence (£sd) currency arithmetics in hardware.

resources.name: Engineering and Operations in the Bell System
resources.desc: Starting at page #445, the "10.5 Billing Equipment and Systems" section describe the history and technical evolutions of Bell's phone calls metering and pricing.

resources.name: The vanished grandeur of accounting
resources.desc: Accounting paintings were a significant genre in Dutch art.

resources.name: Graphic methods for presenting facts
resources.desc: A way to optimize pricing using a physical model made in plaster of Paris, from 1914.

resources.name: Detax
resources.desc: A site mockup of an tax avoidance product for small businesses.

resources.name: Superman III
resources.desc: The 1983 film in which Gus Gorman, a laid-off clerk who retrains as a programmer, embezzles from his employer's payroll by skimming the fractions of a cent it rounds down.
